generations.label: alternate complete CUDA-graph replay; token role unassigned

request_output_evidence.conclusion: Responses prove two output token IDs per sequence, but expose no per-token timestamps or graph identifiers.

server_log_evidence.conclusion: The coarse scheduler row proves B=100 CUDA-graph decode, but does not label either graph as output token 1 or token 2.

graph_correlation_evidence.conclusion: CUPTI ties both generations to real cudaGraphLaunch calls, but CUDA correlation IDs carry no model-token ordinal.

defensible_labels.alternate: alternate complete CUDA-graph replay; token role unassigned
defensible_labels.whole_request: entire matched B=100 request containing two complete CUDA-graph replays

h200_reference_comparison.prior_policy: The first eight-device graph finishes before the matched server Finish lifecycle and produces the one requested computed decode token. The next eight-device graph starts after that useful graph, crosses the Finish boundary, and is retained only as cleanup/steady-body context.
h200_reference_comparison.gb300_transfer_rule: Do not transfer the H200 cleanup label by ordinal. The H200 label had a lifecycle-boundary premise (its second graph crossed Finish); both GB300 generations finish before the matched latest Finish boundary.
